# $(echo .. | tr . -)), a variable carries, or is split across two names.

# --- WU-IAENG-286: the legitimate-command corpus. WU-285 (#112) reported 0
# false positives over a 47-command legitimate corpus, but that corpus was
# never committed, so the headline number was not reproducible — only the
# cases above existed in the suite. These ~37 cases are commands a real
# project genuinely runs, spanning: printf for logging / commit messages /
# ANSI colour; eval of a shell-init hook (ssh-agent, direnv, pyenv, rbenv,
# starship, gh completion); a variable holding a non-forbidden flag; a
# benign $(...) command substitution; an ordinary git push/commit/fetch/
# pull/merge/tag; and grep/sed/awk/find pipelines. Each was verified rc=0
# against the CURRENT hook before being added here — none of these is
# asserting a false expectation. Re-run on every CI, this is what keeps
# "0 false positives" a property of the hook rather than a one-time claim.

git commit -m "feat(api): add pagination" -m "Longer body explaining why."
